name: manual_c06864
claim: When consolidating append-only JSONL memory files across branches, never use naive bash tools like 'sort -u' or key-based JSON deduplication, which can mangle text or drop legacy schema entries. Instead, perform a strict, lossless string-level union against the untouched canonical base (e.g. origin/main) in an isolated staging area to ensure zero data loss.

decisions.notes: A previous memory merge attempt used 'cat | sort -u' and a naive Python key-parser that accidentally deleted 600+ legacy episodic memory lines. Append-only logs require strictly additive, lossless merging methods.

PR #354 CodeRabbit nitpick (review 4945045084): conditions was a bag-of-words copy of the claim, including stopwords (across, against, which, zero) with no discriminative value for retrieval.
